title: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Kings 5](/bible/2-kings/5)

**[2 Kings 5:1-4](/bible/2-kings/5#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/2-kings/5#v1)</sup> Now Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the Lord had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-kings/5#v2)</sup> And the Syrians had gone out by companies, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid; and she waited on Naaman’s wife.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-kings/5#v3)</sup> And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-kings/5#v4)</sup> And one went in, and told his lord, saying, Thus and thus said the maid that is of the land of Israel.

- Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, is a great man with his master and honorable, because by him the Lord had given deliverance to Syria. He is a mighty man of valor, but he is a leper.
- The Syrians had gone out by companies and brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid, and she waits on Naaman's wife. This maid is an Israelite sister serving in a foreign house.
- She tells her mistress that if only her lord were with the prophet in Samaria, he would recover him of his leprosy. Naaman goes and tells his lord what the maid of Israel said.

**[2 Kings 5:5-7](/bible/2-kings/5#v5)**
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-kings/5#v5)</sup> And the king of Syria said, Go to, go, and I will send a letter unto the king of Israel. And he departed, and took with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-kings/5#v6)</sup> And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, Now when this letter is come unto thee, behold, I have therewith sent Naaman my servant to thee, that thou mayest recover him of his leprosy.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-kings/5#v7)</sup> And it came to pass, when the king of Israel had read the letter, that he rent his clothes, and said, Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy? wherefore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarrel against me.

- The king of Syria sends Naaman with a letter to the king of Israel, and Naaman takes ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment. The letter asks the king of Israel to recover Naaman of his leprosy.
- When the king of Israel reads the letter, he rends his clothes and asks, am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to recover a man of his leprosy. He thinks the king of Syria is seeking a quarrel against him, knowing he has no such power.

**[2 Kings 5:8-10](/bible/2-kings/5#v8)**
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-kings/5#v8)</sup> And it was so, when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-kings/5#v9)</sup> So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-kings/5#v10)</sup> And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

- When Elisha the man of God hears that the king of Israel has rent his clothes, he sends to the king asking why, and says let the man come to him, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.
- Naaman comes with his horses and chariot and stands at the door of Elisha's house. Elisha sends a messenger out to him, saying go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

**[2 Kings 5:11-14](/bible/2-kings/5#v11)**
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-kings/5#v11)</sup> But Naaman was wroth, and went away, and said, Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the Lord his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-kings/5#v12)</sup> Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-kings/5#v13)</sup> And his servants came near, and spake unto him, and said, My father, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean?
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-kings/5#v14)</sup> Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

- Naaman is wroth and goes away, saying he thought the prophet would surely come out to him, stand, call on the name of the Lord his God, strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper. He complains in his pride that this was not the process he expected.
- He asks whether Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, are not better than all the waters of Israel, and turns away in a rage, thinking of a physical cleansing rather than a spiritual one. His mind is carnal, not thinking as the prophet thinks.
- His servants come near and reason with him, that if the prophet had bidden him do some great thing he would have done it; how much rather then when he says only wash and be clean. Taking heed, Naaman goes down and dips himself seven times in Jordan according to the saying of the man of God, and his flesh comes again like the flesh of a little child, and he is clean.

**[2 Kings 5:15-19](/bible/2-kings/5#v15)**
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-kings/5#v15)</sup> And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-kings/5#v16)</sup> But he said, As the Lord liveth, before whom I stand, I will receive none. And he urged him to take it; but he refused.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-kings/5#v17)</sup> And Naaman said, Shall there not then, I pray thee, be given to thy servant two mules’ burden of earth? for thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, but unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-kings/5#v18)</sup> In this thing the Lord pardon thy servant, that when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the Lord pardon thy servant in this thing.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-kings/5#v19)</sup> And he said unto him, Go in peace. So he departed from him a little way.

- Naaman returns to the man of God with all his company and stands before him, saying, behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. He asks Elisha to take a blessing of his servant.
- Elisha says, as the Lord liveth before whom I stand, I will receive none, and though Naaman urges him, he refuses. Naaman asks that he be given two mules' burden of earth, for from now on he will offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods but to the Lord.
- He asks that the Lord pardon him in one thing, that when his master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship and leans on his hand, and he bows there, the Lord pardon his servant. Elisha says, go in peace, and Naaman departs a little way.

**[2 Kings 5:20-24](/bible/2-kings/5#v20)**
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-kings/5#v20)</sup> But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, Behold, my master hath spared Naaman this Syrian, in not receiving at his hands that which he brought: but, as the Lord liveth, I will run after him, and take somewhat of him.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-kings/5#v21)</sup> So Gehazi followed after Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running after him, he lighted down from the chariot to meet him, and said, Is all well?
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-kings/5#v22)</sup> And he said, All is well. My master hath sent me, saying, Behold, even now there be come to me from mount Ephraim two young men of the sons of the prophets: give them, I pray thee, a talent of silver, and two changes of garments.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-kings/5#v23)</sup> And Naaman said, Be content, take two talents. And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and laid them upon two of his servants; and they bare them before him.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/2-kings/5#v24)</sup> And when he came to the tower, he took them from their hand, and bestowed them in the house: and he let the men go, and they departed.

- Gehazi, the servant of Elisha, reasons that his master has spared Naaman the Syrian by not receiving what he brought, and swears, as the Lord liveth, he will run after him and take somewhat of him. When Naaman sees him running, he lights down from the chariot to meet him and asks whether all is well.
- Gehazi lies, saying his master has sent him, that two young men of the sons of the prophets have come from mount Ephraim, and asks for a talent of silver and two changes of garments. Naaman urges him to take two talents, binds them in two bags with two changes of garments, and lays them on two of his servants to carry before Gehazi.
- When Gehazi comes to the tower, he takes the goods from their hand, bestows them in the house, and sends the men away, hiding what he took like a thief.

**[2 Kings 5:25-27](/bible/2-kings/5#v25)**
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-kings/5#v25)</sup> But he went in, and stood before his master. And Elisha said unto him, Whence comest thou, Gehazi? And he said, Thy servant went no whither.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/2-kings/5#v26)</sup> And he said unto him, Went not mine heart with thee, when the man turned again from his chariot to meet thee? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants?
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-kings/5#v27)</sup> The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence a leper as white as snow.

- Gehazi goes in and stands before his master, and Elisha asks where he has come from, and Gehazi says his servant went nowhere. Elisha says, went not my heart with thee when the man turned from his chariot to meet thee; is it a time to receive money, garments, oliveyards, vineyards, sheep, oxen, menservants, and maidservants.
- Because Gehazi took in a time that was not the time to receive, the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to him and to his seed forever, and he goes out from Elisha's presence a leper as white as snow. This shows how Israel thought then and how the nation still thinks now, hasty to grasp things by unjust means.
  - **[Ecclesiastes 3:1](/bible/ecclesiastes/3#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/ecclesiastes/3#v1)</sup> To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:

    To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.
  - **[Ecclesiastes 3:6](/bible/ecclesiastes/3#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/ecclesiastes/3#v6)</sup> A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

    There is a time to get, and a time to lose, which is what Elisha explained to Gehazi, that there was a time to receive the gifts and this was not it.
